title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 14
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'ground-to-grid' (G2G) correction accounts for:
options: Map projection distortion and elevation difference
questions.solution: G2G = grid factor × combined factor; it converts measured ground distance/bearing to grid values.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An error that has a definite sign and magnitude is called:
questions.solution: Systematic errors follow a physical law and can be corrected (e.g., collimation error).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Random errors are also known as:
questions.solution: Random (accidental) errors arise from unpredictable fluctuations and follow the normal distribution.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'blunder' in surveying is:
options: A mistake due to carelessness, e.g., misreading a tape
questions.solution: Blunders (gross errors) are mistakes from human carelessness and should be detected and removed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A rescue room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed belowground exceeds 100 and:
options: The mine produces less than 100 tonnes a day
There is no rescue station within 35 km
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue room is required when more than 100 persons work belowground and no rescue station is within 35 km.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'standard deviation' of a set of observations measures:
options: The spread or dispersion of observations about the mean
questions.solution: Standard deviation σ quantifies the scatter of observations; smaller σ means more precise measurements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For n observations, the 'degrees of freedom' in computing standard deviation is:
questions.solution: Using n-1 (Bessel's correction) gives an unbiased estimate of the population variance from a sample.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'most probable value' of a set of equal-precision observations is their:
questions.solution: For equal-weight observations, the arithmetic mean minimises the sum of squared residuals.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A person re-employed after an absence exceeding one year from mining work must undergo refresher training within:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 10: refresher training within 1 month of re-employment after absence over 1 year.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'sum of residuals' for a set of observations is always:
questions.solution: By definition, Σv = Σ(lᵢ - x̄) = 0 when x̄ is the arithmetic mean.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'variance' is the square of:
questions.solution: Variance σ² = (Σv²)/(n-1); standard deviation σ = √(variance).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'standard error of the mean' is:
questions.solution: Standard error of the mean = σ/√n; it decreases as more observations are taken.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: According to the '68-95-99.7 rule', approximately 95% of observations lie within:
questions.solution: About 95.4% of normally distributed data falls within ±2σ of the mean.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'probable error' of a single observation is approximately:
questions.solution: Probable error = 0.6745σ; it divides the distribution into equal halves.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, the breathing apparatus kept at a rescue station or rescue room shall:
options: Be of the same type and make
Be of different types for flexibility
questions.solution: MRR 1985, Rule 11(4): breathing apparatus at a rescue station/room must be of the same type and make for interchangeability.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In least squares adjustment, the quantity minimised is:
questions.solution: Least squares minimises Σv², giving the best-fit solution in the minimum squares sense.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'chi-square' test is used to test:
options: Whether the mean equals a specific value
Whether variance differs from a hypothesised value
Whether observations follow a normal distribution
The goodness of fit of a distribution
questions.solution: Chi-square tests can assess normality, goodness of fit, and variance hypotheses.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 't-distribution' is used instead of the normal distribution when:
options: The population standard deviation is unknown and the sample is small
questions.solution: The t-distribution accounts for the additional uncertainty when σ is estimated from a small sample.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As the sample size increases, the t-distribution approaches:
questions.solution: With increasing degrees of freedom, the t-distribution converges to the standard normal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'number of degrees of freedom' in a least squares adjustment is:
options: Number of observations minus number of unknowns
Number of observations plus number of unknowns
questions.solution: DOF = n - u; redundancy (DOF) must be ≥ 1 for adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'misclosure' in a traverse is the:
options: Difference between the starting and ending coordinates
questions.solution: Misclosure = difference between computed and known end position; it quantifies the traverse error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'precision' of measurements refers to:
options: Closeness of repeated measurements to each other
questions.solution: Precision is the reproducibility of measurements; accuracy is closeness to truth.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A measurement can be precise but not accurate if:
questions.solution: Systematic errors cause biased (inaccurate) results even when random scatter is small (high precision).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, a rescue station shall be under the charge of a Superintendent assisted by at least:
options: 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue station has a Superintendent, at least 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'outlier' is an observation that:
questions.solution: An outlier is a value that deviates markedly from the majority, suggesting a possible blunder.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Chauvenet criterion' is used to:
options: Detect outliers and decide whether to reject them
questions.solution: Chauvenet's criterion provides a probabilistic threshold for rejecting suspected outliers.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'propagation of errors' law states that for z = f(x, y), the variance of z is:
questions.solution: The general law of propagation of variances: σ²_z = Σ(∂f/∂xᵢ)²σ²_xᵢ for independent variables.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If two measurements are correlated, the covariance term in error propagation:
options: Must be included in the variance computation
questions.solution: For correlated observations: σ²_z = Σ(∂f/∂xᵢ)²σ²_xᵢ + 2Σ(∂f/∂xᵢ)(∂f/∂xⱼ)Cov(xᵢ,xⱼ).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'weight' of an observation is:
questions.solution: Weight pᵢ ∝ 1/σ²_i; more precise observations receive higher weights.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In weighted least squares, the weighted mean is:
questions.solution: Weighted mean x̄ = Σ(pᵢlᵢ)/Σpᵢ; observations with higher weight contribute more.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'redundancy' in a survey is:
options: The number of observations minus the number of unknowns
questions.solution: Redundancy = DOF = n - u; it allows error detection and adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per MVTR 1966, refresher vocational training must be given to persons employed in mines at least once in:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 8: refresher training at least once in every 5 years.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'a priori' standard deviation is:
options: Assumed before the adjustment based on expected accuracy
questions.solution: A priori σ₀ is estimated from expected instrument accuracy before the adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'a posteriori' standard deviation is:
options: Always equal to the a priori value
Computed from the adjustment residuals after the least squares solution
questions.solution: A posteriori σ₀ = √(v̂ᵀPv̂/DOF); it reflects the actual residuals from the adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'reference variance factor' (σ²₀) in least squares is estimated as:
questions.solution: σ̂²₀ = v̂ᵀPv̂ / DOF, where DOF = n - u.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'blunder detection' method based on redundancy is:
questions.solution: Baarda's data snooping tests each residual against a threshold to detect gross errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'internal reliability' of a network refers to:
questions.solution: Internal reliability is the network's ability to detect its own gross errors through redundancy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'external reliability' of a network refers to:
options: The impact of undetected blunders on the coordinates
questions.solution: External reliability quantifies how much an undetected blunder would distort the final result.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966, a person before being employed in a mine for the first time must undergo:
options: Initial vocational training in the prescribed subjects
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 6: every person is given initial vocational training before first employment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'law of propagation of covariances' in matrix form is:
questions.solution: Where J is the Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives ∂f/∂x.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'weighted residual' is:
questions.solution: Weighted residual = vᵢ × pᵢ; in data snooping, the normalised residual is vᵢ√pᵢ / σ₀.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Baarda data snooping' test statistic is:
questions.solution: w_i = v̂_i√p_i / σ̂₀ is compared against a critical value from the normal distribution.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the a posteriori variance factor differs significantly from the a priori value, it suggests:
options: The a priori variance estimate or the stochastic model may be wrong
questions.solution: A significant discrepancy indicates the assumed σ₀ or the weight matrix P may be incorrect.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'F-test' in least squares is used to:
questions.solution: The F-test compares two variance ratios; it is used to test if two populations have equal variances.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a traverse, the 'angular misclosure' is distributed by:
options: Adjusting angles equally (Compass rule for angles)
Distributing the linear misclosure by angles
questions.solution: Angular misclosure is typically distributed equally among all measured angles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Plans and sections required under CMR 2017 shall be corrected and maintained up-to-date at intervals not exceeding:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(4): plans are kept corrected up-to-date not earlier than 3 months.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Transit rule' for traverse adjustment distributes linear misclosure:
options: Proportional to the latitude/projection of each side
questions.solution: Transit rule: correction ∝ latitude (or departure) of each side, rather than its length.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Unless otherwise approved, mine plans and sections under CMR 2017 shall be prepared on a scale with a representative factor of:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(1)(d): plans are on a scale with RF 2000:1 or 1000:1, with a scale bar at least 25 cm long.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'correction' to an observation has the same magnitude but opposite sign as the:
questions.solution: True error = correction + residual (in practice, correction ≈ -residual for small errors).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Photogrammetry is the science of making measurements from:
questions.solution: Photogrammetry extracts 3D information from 2D images.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'metric camera' is calibrated to have:
options: Known and stable interior orientation parameters
questions.solution: Metric cameras have precisely known focal length, principal point, and lens distortion parameters.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'focal length' of a camera lens is the distance from the:
options: Centre of the lens to the focal plane (image)
Two nodal points of the lens
questions.solution: Focal length f is the distance from the optical centre to the image plane when focused at infinity.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'principal point' of a photograph is:
options: The intersection of the perpendicular from the lens centre to the image plane
questions.solution: The principal point is where the optical axis intersects the image plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'fiducial marks' on a metric camera are used to:
options: Define the coordinate system of the photograph
questions.solution: Fiducial marks (typically 4 or 8) define the photo coordinate system.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A shot-firer who has not been employed in blasting duties for more than 6 months shall undergo:
options: Retraining in the handling of explosives before resuming such duties
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 13: retraining in handling of explosives is required after an absence from such duties exceeding 6 months.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'vertical photograph' has the camera axis:
options: As nearly vertical as possible, within ~3° of plumb
questions.solution: A 'vertical' photo is nominally vertical but may have a slight tilt (typically < 3°).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per DGMS Circular 2/2010, strata and dump slope monitoring is mandatory for dumps exceeding ______ in height.
questions.solution: DGMS Circular 2/2010: monitoring (including slope stability radar / real-time monitoring) is made mandatory for dumps exceeding 60 m height.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'scale' of a vertical photograph at a point is:
questions.solution: Scale s = f / (H - h), where f = focal length, H = flying height above datum, h = ground elevation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The flying height H in the scale formula is measured from:
options: The camera to the ground vertically
questions.solution: H is the height of the exposure station above the datum (usually MSL).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'parallax' in stereo vision is the:
options: Difference in position of a point on two overlapping photos
questions.solution: Parallax p = x_left - x_right; it is used to determine height (relative elevation).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'parallax formula' for elevation is:
questions.solution: Elevation h = H - Bf/p, where B = air base, f = focal length, p = parallax.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'air base' (B) is the:
options: Distance between two successive exposure stations
questions.solution: Air base B is the horizontal distance between consecutive camera stations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For stereo overlap, the standard forward overlap is:
questions.solution: 60% forward overlap (and 30% side overlap) is standard for aerial photography.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'stereoscope' is used to:
options: View two overlapping photos in 3D (stereo model)
questions.solution: A stereoscope creates a 3D perception from a stereo pair of overlapping photographs.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'anaglyph' is a stereo pair viewed with:
questions.solution: Anaglyphs use colour-filtered glasses (typically red/cyan) to separate left and right images.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 of 2010 deals with:
options: Design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines
questions.solution: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 dated 06.07.2010 concerns design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'digital elevation model' (DEM) is:
options: A regular grid of elevation values
questions.solution: A DEM is a raster (grid) of elevation values representing the terrain surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'digital surface model' (DSM) includes:
options: Bare earth plus buildings and vegetation
questions.solution: DSM captures the top of all features (roofs, trees), unlike DTM which is bare earth only.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'orthophoto' is:
options: A photograph corrected for terrain displacement and tilt to have uniform scale
questions.solution: Orthorectification removes terrain and tilt distortions, creating a photo with map-like geometry.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: LiDAR stands for:
questions.solution: LiDAR = Light Detection And Ranging; uses laser pulses to measure distances.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A LiDAR point cloud is:
options: A large collection of 3D points from laser returns
questions.solution: LiDAR produces dense 3D point clouds with x, y, z and intensity values.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'ground sampling distance' (GSD) in aerial photography is:
options: The ground area represented by one pixel
questions.solution: GSD is the ground distance between pixel centres; smaller GSD = higher resolution.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For drone survey planning, the GSD is determined by:
options: Flying height, focal length, and sensor pixel size
questions.solution: GSD = (pixel size × flying height) / focal length.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A rescue-trained person shall practise with breathing apparatus at least:
options: 8 times a year, of which 4 in mines
4 times a year, of which 2 in mines
questions.solution: MRR 1985: rescue-trained persons practise with breathing apparatus at least 8 times a year, including 4 practices in the mine.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'interior orientation' parameters of a camera include:
options: Focal length, principal point, and lens distortion
questions.solution: Interior orientation defines the internal geometry of the camera.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'exterior orientation' of a photo specifies:
options: The position and orientation of the camera in space at exposure
questions.solution: Exterior orientation = 3 position (X₀, Y₀, Z₀) and 3 rotation (ω, φ, κ) parameters.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The six exterior orientation parameters are:
options: Three focal lengths and three distortions
questions.solution: X₀, Y₀, Z₀ (position) and ω, φ, κ (rotation angles about the axes).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Omega-Phi-Kappa' rotation system rotates the photo about:
options: X, Y, Z axes of the photo coordinate system
questions.solution: ω (roll) about X-axis, φ (pitch) about Y-axis, κ (yaw) about Z-axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'ground control point' (GCP) is:
options: A point identified on the photo only
A point with known ground coordinates used for orientation
questions.solution: GCPs have precisely known ground coordinates and are identified on photos for georeferencing.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In drone photogrammetry, 'structure from motion' (SfM) is:
options: A technique to measure building heights
A method to reconstruct 3D structure from overlapping 2D images
questions.solution: SfM automatically matches features across images to build 3D point clouds and camera positions.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A product is bought at 10% discount on marked price and sold at 10% above marked price. What is the gain percent on the cost price?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 5:7. If B is 28 years old, what is A's age?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: How many times do the hands of a clock form a right angle in a day?
questions.solution: The hands are at right angle 22 times in 12 hours. So 44 times in 24 hours

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: How many times does the 29th of a month occur in 400 years?
questions.solution: In 400 years: 97 leap years. So 29 Feb occurs 97 times. Total 29th of any month = 12×400 - 97 = 4497... Actually: 400 years have 4800 months. 97 of those are Feb in leap years. So 29th occurs 4800 - 97 = 4703... Let me recalculate. Every month has a 29th. In 400 years = 4800 months. But Feb in non-leap years only has 28 days. Non-leap Feb = 400 - 97 = 303. So 29th occurs 4800 - 303 = 4497 times.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G are standing in a line. A is third from left. B is to the right of A. C is immediately to the left of B. D is at the extreme right. E is between A and B. Who is immediately to the right of E?
questions.solution: Arrangement: _,_,A,E,_,B,C with D at right end. B is right of E.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution: Kosi river is known as the Sorrow of Bihar due to frequent floods.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The southernmost point of India is located in which state/UT?
questions.solution: Indira Point in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.solution: Zoji La connects Srinagar with Leh in Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.solution: Tropic of Cancer passes through Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram — but not Odisha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the largest saltwater lake in India?
questions.solution: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest saltwater lake in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.solution: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which of the following is the highest peak in South India?
questions.solution: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in South India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which canal connects the Bay of Bengal with the Arabian Sea through India?
questions.solution: Indira Gandhi Canal is the longest canal in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.solution: Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution: Black (regur) soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.solution: Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass is known as the 'Gateway to the North-East'?
questions.solution: Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck) connects mainland India to the North-East.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state receives rainfall from both the Southwest and Northeast monsoons?
questions.solution: Tamil Nadu receives rainfall from both Southwest (partial) and Northeast monsoons.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The maximum area under forest cover in India is in which state?
questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in India by area.
